newsitem.title: ITALY: ENI sees first-half profits up 5.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: ENI sees first-half profits up 5.5 pct.

text.p: Italian energy giant ENI, which is due to offer a second tranche of its shares to investors in late October, on Tuesday reported a 5.5 percent rise in first half 1996 net profits boosted by rising oil and natural gas income.

The oil and chemicals group, which currently has 15 percent of its shares quoted, reported first half consolidated net profits of 2.758 trillion lire ($1.8 billion) against 2.615 trillion lire in the first half of 1995.
The group has moved to using U.S. accounting system SFAS 121 and reported its first-half net profit at 2.376 trillion lire under the system, while no comparison was available.

The group floated 15 percent of its shares to trade in Milan, London and New York last November at 5,250 lire a share and the share price has since climbed to close Tuesday on the Milan bourse up 0.07 percent at 7,001 lire a share.

ENI said its operating profits from oil and natural gas rose 11 percent, but profits from its chemical activities fell reflecting difficult trading conditions in the European chemical market and the appreciation of the lira.
The state-controlled group said that profits had also been helped by the 31 percent fall in interest charges after its net debt slipped to 15.078 trillion lire from 17.795 trillion lire.

The fall in the debt came after paying a dividend of 1.7 trillion lire by the parent company ENI SpA and after making group investments of 3.293 trillion lire -- of which 91 percent were focused on oil and natural gas activities.

ENI, which is Italy's largest listed company although only 15 percent of its shares are quoted, said that its restructuring programme aimed at focusing on its core activities and the selling-off of non-strategic assets would be completed during 1996. ($1=1,523 lire)
